review_notes:
I read all of WeightedChainMetric.lean (lines 1–118). I also read the definitions and lemmas it depends on in Analysis/CompactWordCost.lean (metricGroupNorm, compactWordCost, compactWeightedNorm, wordLength_le_weightedNorm_add, metric_le_compactWordCost) and Analysis/CompactGeneratingBalls.lean (wordLength_ball_subset_pow, isCompact_set_pow). Its only downstream user, Geometry/WeightedMetricChains.lean, I checked too. In Mathlib I checked the instance needed by `Continuous.mul` / `continuous_mul`, which is `ContinuousMul`.

Other things I considered and rejected:
- `hδ1 : δ ≤ 1` is genuinely needed through wordLength_le_weightedNorm_add.
- `hbounded` (metric bounded by 1) is a structural assumption built into `compactWeightedNorm` upstream. Weakening it would mean changing other files, not this one.
- `hδ` and `hball` are each used where they are included.
- `weightedDistance_le_near`, `metric_le_weightedDistance`, `weightedDistance_topology` and `weightedGroupMetric_isometric` already use only the assumptions their proofs need.

Remaining uncertainty: I have not compiled the proposed weakening. The argument rests on the instance requirements of the lemmas I read.

findings.problem:
The theorem asks for `[IsTopologicalGroup G]`, but the proof only uses continuity of multiplication. It uses that in two places:
- `isCompact_set_pow K hcompact n`, which is stated with only `[TopologicalSpace G] [ContinuousMul G]`;
- `continuous_const.mul continuous_id`, which comes from Mathlib's `Continuous.mul` under `[ContinuousMul M]`.

Nothing in the proof uses continuity of inversion. Requiring `IsTopologicalGroup` therefore makes users supply a `ContinuousInv` instance that the result does not need.
findings.proposed_change:
Weaken the instance argument:

```lean
include hδ1 in
theorem weightedGroupMetric_proper [ContinuousMul G] (hcompact : IsCompact K) :
    letI := weightedGroupMetric K hK hsymm hbounded δ hδ hball
    ProperSpace G := by
  -- proof unchanged
```

The proof body can stay as it is:
- `isCompact_set_pow` already elaborates with `ContinuousMul G`.
- `(hcompactPow _).image (continuous_const.mul continuous_id)` uses `Continuous.mul`, which only needs `ContinuousMul`.
- The rest of the proof (`weighted_ball_subset_compact_power`, `isClosed_closedBall`, `map_inv_eq_map`) uses no topological-group structure.

The binder `[IsTopologicalGroup G]` in `weightedProperChainMetric` (WeightedMetricChains.lean) could then be weakened in the same way. Any `IsTopologicalGroup G` instance still provides `ContinuousMul G`, so existing call sites keep working.
findings.benefit: The statement now asks only for what the proof uses. A user who has a monoid-level `ContinuousMul` instance on a group with a left-invariant metric no longer has to prove that inversion is continuous first. (With `IsIsometricSMul G G`, inversion is in fact automatically continuous, so the extra assumption gives the user nothing.) Readers can also see that properness of the weighted metric depends only on `K ^ n` being compact, not on topological-group structure.

theorem isCompact_set_pow [TopologicalSpace G] [ContinuousMul G]
    (hcompact : IsCompact K) (n : ℕ) : IsCompact (K ^ n) := by

theorem Continuous.mul (hf : Continuous f) (hg : Continuous g) :
    Continuous (f * g) :=
  continuous_mul.comp₂ hf hg
